brand.name: InforMed
brand.tagline: Science-backed health, explained like a friend would.
brand.mission: Build a trusted community around science-based health facts: integrity, empowerment, compassion, innovation and transparency.

audience.description: English-speaking adults 25-65, mostly US/UK/CA/AU: people on or considering GLP-1 medicines (Ozempic, Wegovy, Mounjaro, Zepbound), people with overweight, obesity, prediabetes or type 2 diabetes, and anyone curious about metabolic health. They want clear, encouraging, science-backed answers.

schedule._comment: Local times in audience.timezone ("+1" = next day). Each piece posts at the same time on every platform of its kind: short = YouTube Shorts + Instagram Reels + TikTok + Facebook Reels; carousel = Instagram + Facebook + TikTok (photo) + Threads; long = YouTube, spaced 8 hours apart so the videos don't compete for each other's reach.

voice._comment: provider: elevenlabs (best, paid) | chatterbox (free, expressive) | kokoro (free, fast). Falls back down that list automatically if one fails.

elevenlabs._voiceComment: 'Jeremy' (friendly, casual American 'guy next door', built for social media/podcasts), chosen by the owner. Any ElevenLabs Voice Library ID works here.
elevenlabs._budgetComment: Starter = 40,000 credits/month. useFor: which content gets ElevenLabs (short, long). A piece only uses ElevenLabs if its whole narration fits the remaining monthly budget; otherwise Chatterbox. eleven_flash_v2_5 costs 0.5 credits/char (set creditsPerChar 0.5).

video._comment: Animated cartoon style only (see docs/STYLE.md). theme: vibrant (Kurzgesagt-like) | doodle (hand-drawn whiteboard look).

safety.policy: Auto-publish only when the Fact-Checker agent returns PASS. Anything else is held and a GitHub issue is opened for human review.
safety.disclaimer: This content is for educational purposes only and is not medical advice. Always talk to a qualified healthcare professional about your own situation.
bannedTopics: cures for cancer or other serious disease
eating disorder encouragement or extreme dieting
buying GLP-1 medicines without a prescription or from compounded, gray-market or research-chemical sources

models._comment: Claude Code model aliases or full IDs. Opus for thinking-heavy work (research, scripts, fact-checks, titles); Sonnet for high-volume visual and polish work, which uses far less of the subscription's usage limits.

music._comment: library: reuse tracks in assets/music/<mood>/ (generate once with `npm run music:library`, cheapest) | elevenlabs: fresh Eleven Music score per video | generated: free built-in synth

prompts.wonder: Warm ambient synth score for an animated science documentary, soft evolving pads, gentle plucked arpeggios, sense of wonder and discovery, 90 bpm, no vocals, no drums until the midpoint, cinematic and uplifting
prompts.curious: Playful curious ambient electronic score for an animated explainer, light marimba and synth plucks, soft pads, subtle percussion, 100 bpm, no vocals
prompts.tense: Tense cinematic synth underscore for an animated medical story, pulsing low synths, ticking percussion, rising strings, 95 bpm, no vocals, suspenseful but not horror
prompts.hopeful: Hopeful uplifting cinematic synth and piano score for an animated health documentary, warm pads, steady gentle pulse, emotional build, 92 bpm, no vocals
prompts.dark: Dark mysterious ambient score, deep drones, sparse piano notes, slow evolving textures, 70 bpm, no vocals

sfx._comment: kit: assets/sfx/<name>/*.mp3 made once with `npm run sfx:kit` (ElevenLabs), falling back to the built-in synth per sound | synth: built-in only

qa._comment: Whisper checks every narrated scene against the script (retakes bad ones) and the final mix for masking; the Visual Critic reviews key frames and sends weak shots back to the Motion Designer.

review._comment: auto: the Editor-in-Chief agent makes the final publish/drop call on held content (owner gets Telegram FYIs with a veto button). human: held content waits for Approve/Reject.

niche._comment: Current editorial focus. Every agent reads this; the trend radar searches these sources. Set enabled=false to go back to general health.
niche.name: GLP-1
niche.brief: The channel currently focuses on GLP-1 medicines (semaglutide: Ozempic, Wegovy, Rybelsus; tirzepatide: Mounjaro, Zepbound; liraglutide; new ones such as orforglipron and retatrutide) and the body's own GLP-1 hormone. Tone: positive and encouraging. We explain what GLP-1 is, how it works in the body, the benefits the evidence supports, who it can help and why someone might want to discuss it with their doctor, and how to get the most out of it (protein, strength training, hydration, eating habits, and making common side effects easier). Every piece stays evidence-based and passes the fact-checker.
pillars: How GLP-1 works: the gut hormone, appetite and 'food noise', insulin and blood sugar, gastric emptying, the brain's reward system
Weight-loss results in the big trials (STEP, SURMOUNT) explained simply, and what keeps results going

Benefits beyond weight: heart attack and stroke risk (SELECT), kidneys (FLOW), fatty liver (MASH), sleep apnea, blood pressure, type 2 diabetes control, and promising early research (addiction, alcohol, inflammation, brain health)
Who it's approved for and who may benefit: questions to bring to your doctor
Getting the most from GLP-1: protein and muscle, strength training, hydration, fibre, eating slower, managing nausea and other common side effects
Life on GLP-1: habits, meal ideas, mindset, keeping results after stopping
Myths and misunderstandings, corrected with evidence (always in a positive, helpful tone)
Natural ways to support your own GLP-1: protein, fibre, eating order, movement (without claiming they replace the medicine)
New GLP-1 research and approvals: what's coming (pills, next-generation drugs)
guardrails: It's a prescription medicine: every script and caption carries a short 'talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you' line.

Positive framing, never false: only benefits the evidence supports, with the right population (e.g. SELECT = adults with heart disease and overweight/obesity). Mention the common side effects briefly and helpfully when relevant.
No dosing or titration instructions, no switching or stopping advice, no 'microdosing' protocols.
Never promote compounded, gray-market, research-chemical or online no-prescription sources.
No before/after body shaming, no extreme-diet messaging; weight is one health measure among many.
Talk about the medicines generically (GLP-1 / semaglutide / tirzepatide); brand names only for recognition, never as ads.

spacing._comment: Minimum hours between two pieces of the same kind on a platform. Enforced when slots are assigned and again right before posting, so late production, backlog or catch-up can never bunch posts.
